_comment: Illustrative, extensible clinical consistency rules for synthetic NCCR CTC (registry) cohorts generated from published marginals. These are STARTER rules meant to be reviewed and expanded with clinician input at the Jamboree. They encode two well-known relationships: (1) prostate-specific markers do not apply to female patients, and (2) retinoblastoma is a cancer of early childhood. Note: prostate-marker record counts in the NCCR metadata are conditional on the prostate-cancer subpopulation, so independent marginal sampling otherwise assigns a Gleason/PSA value to every synthetic record.

constraints.name: gleason_clinical_score_is_male_only
constraints.description: Gleason score (prostate) does not apply to female patients.

constraints.name: gleason_pathologic_score_is_male_only
constraints.description: Gleason score (prostate) does not apply to female patients.

constraints.name: gleason_clinical_pattern_is_male_only
constraints.description: Gleason pattern (prostate) does not apply to female patients.

constraints.name: gleason_pathologic_pattern_is_male_only
constraints.description: Gleason pattern (prostate) does not apply to female patients.

constraints.name: gleason_tertiary_pattern_is_male_only
constraints.description: Gleason tertiary pattern (prostate) does not apply to female patients.

constraints.name: psa_is_male_only
constraints.description: PSA (prostate-specific antigen) does not apply to female patients.

constraints.name: retinoblastoma_is_early_childhood
constraints.description: Retinoblastoma occurs almost exclusively in early childhood (typically under 5).
